scope: Host elapsed microseconds with GET_USEC_TIM and pure GET_USEC_SUB

reference_basis.documented: INTEGER microsecond sampling, value-returning GET_USEC_SUB(later,earlier), and a two-minute measurement limit
reference_basis.uncertainty: Native encoding, epoch, exact overflow and tick precision are unverified; GET_USEC_SUB heading says procedure but signature, return type and example use a function

implementation_choices.clock: Default time.monotonic_ns() // 1000, sampled only at evaluated GET_USEC_TIM sites, modulo 120000000; no calendar clock
implementation_choices.adapter: Optional Program(clock_us=...) synchronous nonnegative Python integer microseconds; allow unbounded samples before modulo, reject bool/float/negative/asynchronous responses; adapter owns progression and is retained across runs
implementation_choices.counter: Portable ring 0..119999999, not a native counter encoding claim
implementation_choices.subtraction: Both INTEGER counter inputs in portable range; (later-earlier) modulo 120000000; elapsed interpretation requires one clock and actual interval shorter than two minutes; multiple wraps/backward or mixed clocks cannot be detected
implementation_choices.effects: Arguments once left-to-right before range checks; ordinary short circuiting, initialization, FOR guards, step budgets and frame cleanup; prior effects retained and pending assignment preserved on errors; sticky ABORT wins
implementation_choices.observations: Program.clock_reads returns defensive line/adapter/outcome records, plus counter on success, reset at run start; no raw unbounded samples in trace
implementation_choices.names: Pythonic fallbacks preserve internal routines; GET_USEC_TIM bare value syntax resolves only after ordinary declarations and USING fields
implementation_choices.reports: Source-located microsecond_timers, microsecond_timer_policy and transitive potential_host_clock_reads routine effects

retained_boundaries: GET_TIME/SET_TIME use a separate explicit CalendarClock since 0.87.0; no timezone, controller/power-on clock, native tick/overflow/encoding or scheduling equivalence
Synchronous host callbacks may block; step budget is not a wall-clock deadline
No controller contact or native runtime acceptance; existing structural/resource protections remain and strict is future work
